segments.spokenText: Part 3. Preparing a student radio feature. You now have one minute to read questions 21 to 30.
You've brought a draft plan for your radio feature. What's the focus now?
segments.sourceText: You’ve brought a draft plan for your radio feature. What’s the focus now?

segments.spokenText: We started with a general history of the night bus. It sounded too much like a list of dates, so we're focusing on the people who use the last service and what the journey means in their routines.
segments.sourceText: We started with a general history of the night bus. It sounded too much like a list of dates, so we’re focusing on the people who use the last service and what the journey means in their routines.

segments.spokenText: We'd like to include different voices without pretending that three interviews represent everyone who travels at night.
segments.sourceText: We’d like to include different voices without pretending that three interviews represent everyone who travels at night.

segments.spokenText: Good. What sound will help listeners understand the setting?
segments.sourceText: Good. What sound will help listeners understand the setting?

segments.spokenText: We recorded the bus arriving, but the engine overwhelms most of the conversation at the stop. We shouldn't just turn up the voices because that also makes the background louder.
segments.sourceText: We recorded the bus arriving, but the engine overwhelms most of the conversation at the stop. We shouldn’t just turn up the voices because that also makes the background louder.

segments.spokenText: We could use a short arrival sound separately, then conduct the interviews a little way from the road. The sound can establish the scene without sitting under every spoken sentence.
segments.sourceText: We could use a short arrival sound separately, then conduct the interviews a little way from the road. The sound can establish the scene without sitting under every spoken sentence.

segments.spokenText: That would improve clarity. Remember that an atmospheric recording is useful only if it serves the story. You don't need continuous noise to prove you were there.
segments.sourceText: That would improve clarity. Remember that an atmospheric recording is useful only if it serves the story. You don’t need continuous noise to prove you were there.

segments.spokenText: We interviewed one passenger already. He gave a lovely account, but asked not to be identifiable. Could we keep the voice and omit the name?
segments.sourceText: We interviewed one passenger already. He gave a lovely account, but asked not to be identifiable. Could we keep the voice and omit the name?

segments.spokenText: A distinctive voice or workplace detail may still identify him. Discuss the intended use with him and offer an alternative, such as reading an agreed extract with another speaker. Don't assume that removing a name solves every privacy issue.
segments.sourceText: A distinctive voice or workplace detail may still identify him. Discuss the intended use with him and offer an alternative, such as reading an agreed extract with another speaker. Don’t assume that removing a name solves every privacy issue.

segments.spokenText: The transport office offered an official spokesperson. We should include that view, but perhaps not let it be the only explanation of why the timetable changed.
segments.sourceText: The transport office offered an official spokesperson. We should include that view, but perhaps not let it be the only explanation of why the timetable changed.

segments.spokenText: Exactly. Ask which records support the explanation, and compare it with other evidence. Official status is relevant to the speaker's role, not a guarantee that every interpretation is complete.
segments.sourceText: Exactly. Ask which records support the explanation, and compare it with other evidence. Official status is relevant to the speaker’s role, not a guarantee that every interpretation is complete.

segments.spokenText: Our biggest editing problem is that all the interviews are interesting. We have enough for twenty minutes but the assignment allows eight.
segments.sourceText: Our biggest editing problem is that all the interviews are interesting. We have enough for twenty minutes but the assignment allows eight.

segments.spokenText: We need to return to the central question and select material that advances it, even if a favourite anecdote has to go.
segments.sourceText: We need to return to the central question and select material that advances it, even if a favourite anecdote has to go.

segments.spokenText: That's the discipline. Cutting should be guided by purpose, not by whether a sentence is easy to remove without changing your preferred argument.
segments.sourceText: That’s the discipline. Cutting should be guided by purpose, not by whether a sentence is easy to remove without changing your preferred argument.

segments.spokenText: Now look at questions 26 to 30.

We've divided the remaining work into five items. The opening sequence is drafted, but we want to play it to someone who hasn't heard the story. If they can't identify the setting and question, we should revise it.
segments.sourceText: We’ve divided the remaining work into five items. The opening sequence is drafted, but we want to play it to someone who hasn’t heard the story. If they can’t identify the setting and question, we should revise it.

segments.spokenText: The permission for the passenger extract is still unresolved. We'll contact him again before using anything, not treat the earlier interview as blanket consent.
segments.sourceText: The permission for the passenger extract is still unresolved. We’ll contact him again before using anything, not treat the earlier interview as blanket consent.

segments.spokenText: Good. Put that ahead of polishing transitions. A beautifully edited extract you can't use isn't progress towards a finished feature.
segments.sourceText: Good. Put that ahead of polishing transitions. A beautifully edited extract you can’t use isn’t progress towards a finished feature.

segments.spokenText: The transport timetable is checked. We compared the current version with the archived one and confirmed the change date with the office, so that part is complete.
segments.sourceText: The transport timetable is checked. We compared the current version with the archived one and confirmed the change date with the office, so that part is complete.

segments.spokenText: Our long music introduction is another matter. It takes almost a minute, which is too much in an eight-minute programme. We'll remove it and retain only a brief transition where it helps listeners follow the change of scene.
segments.sourceText: Our long music introduction is another matter. It takes almost a minute, which is too much in an eight-minute programme. We’ll remove it and retain only a brief transition where it helps listeners follow the change of scene.

segments.spokenText: Ensure you have rights to whatever music remains. There is no need for a grand opening merely because professional programmes sometimes use one.
segments.sourceText: Ensure you have rights to whatever music remains. There is no need for a grand opening merely because professional programmes sometimes use one.

segments.spokenText: The final title is undecided. We have a working title, but we'll choose the public one after the edit, when we know what the piece actually emphasises.
segments.sourceText: The final title is undecided. We have a working title, but we’ll choose the public one after the edit, when we know what the piece actually emphasises.

segments.spokenText: Otherwise we might force the material to fulfil a clever title we invented before listening properly. We'll keep a few alternatives and ask what each one promises the audience.
segments.sourceText: Otherwise we might force the material to fulfil a clever title we invented before listening properly. We’ll keep a few alternatives and ask what each one promises the audience.

segments.spokenText: Sensible. When you deliver, include a short production note describing major editorial choices. Listeners won't hear every decision, but the note should explain why you selected voices, separated sound from speech and omitted material. It makes the learning visible without turning the feature itself into a lecture about editing.

segments.spokenText: That is the end of part 3. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers.
